correctness.rationale: Translation-invariant Walsh characters diagonalize K(x,y)=q^{h(x,y)^2}; the exact eigenvalues are the Krawtchouk sums. When dq<=2 and q<=1/16, the absolute remainder R_d=sum_{j>=2} C(d,j)q^{j^2} satisfies R_d<q, so every nonparity character eigenvalue exceeds B_d(q) by at least 2(d-k)q-2R_d>0. Alternating-series signs give B_d>0 when d<=floor(1/q), the first possible nonpositive case is d=m+1, and B_{m+2}<0; coordinate subcube inheritance handles all larger d. The derivative tail bound makes the single root q_d unique in (1/d,1/(d-1)) for d>=17. Taylor expansion of B_d gives q_d=1/d+1/(2d^3)+O(d^-4). Independently verified exact parity-minimality in 148 dimension/character cases and high-precision roots for d=17,19,25,40; finite checks do not establish the infinite inequalities.
